latin: Tota substantia animae rationalis est pars intellectualis.
translation: The whole substance of the rational soul is an intellectual part.
translation_note: "pars intellectualis" is terse and its precise sense is not resolved by the located scholarship; kept literal rather than resolved (farmer1998:21257).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch13, from Latin at farmer1998:21257
doctrine: The thesis holds that the whole substance of the rational soul is an intellectual part (farmer1998:21257).
historiography: The German study Erkenntnistheorie und christliche Kabbalah lists the thesis together with 3>60 ("Nihil intelligit actu et distincte anima, nisi se ipsam") and 3>66 in a note on Pico's account of the soul's self-understanding, and separately alongside 3>52 in a note citing Roulier's Jean Pic de la Mirandole and Farmer's own discussion at pages 112-14 of his Syncretism in the West, without further comment on 3>61 itself (kabbalah_paradigma:1695; kabbalah_paradigma:1765).
not_established: Farmer offers no note on this thesis: not established by the sources consulted (farmer1998:21257).
The precise sense of "pars intellectualis" in this thesis: not established by the sources consulted.
